artists.biography:
English drummer and percussionist. He is best known for playing with the British progressive rock bands Porcupine Tree and King Crimson. 
His influences come from his father's jazz collection and from drummers such as Steve Gadd and Jeff Porcaro.
Gavin started to work professionally in 1979. In 1983–84 he toured as a member of Renaissance. He worked as a freelance session drummer on records and tours for the following artists: Incognito, Lisa Stansfield, Lewis Taylor, Artful Dodger, Paul Young, Iggy Pop, Level 42, Porcupine Tree, OSI, King Crimson, Shooter, Dizrhythmia,The Kings Of Oblivion, Sam Brown, Tom Robinson, Go West, Black, Gail Ann Dorsey, B J Cole, Dave Stewart and Barbara Gaskin, Nathan East, Yasuaki Shimizu, Camouflage, Kevin Ayers, Claudio Baglioni, Franco Battiato, Chizuko Yoshihiro, Jakko, Richard Barbieri, Mick Karn, Eros Ramazzotti, Devogue.

perplexity.description:
Cheating the Polygraph, released in 2015 on the Kscope label, is the third solo album by British drummer Gavin Harrison. Known primarily for his work with Porcupine Tree and King Crimson, Harrison uses this album to explore a more jazz-inflected and rhythmically intricate sound, blending progressive rock with elements of jazz fusion and ambient textures. The music is characterized by complex time signatures, subtle dynamics, and a strong emphasis on groove and improvisation, showcasing Harrison’s virtuosic drumming alongside contributions from a rotating cast of guest musicians.

Within Harrison’s discography, Cheating the Polygraph stands out as a deeply personal and experimental project, distinct from his more rock-oriented collaborations. The album received positive critical attention for its sophisticated arrangements and Harrison’s nuanced approach to composition, though it did not achieve major commercial success, peaking at number 73 on the UK Albums Chart. Its release on Kscope, a label known for progressive and art rock, further cemented Harrison’s reputation as a leading figure in the progressive music scene.
